explanation: An induction (repeat-and-copy) head: at token t it attends to the token that immediately followed the most recent earlier occurrence of t's own token (plus the other such followers) and copies it, so a repeated word, word piece, identifier, code directive or template slot is active at its second and later occurrences — repeated templates and code lines, Katakana/Indic byte-sequence words and repeats of distinctive words reach 0.3-0.6x max, though repeats whose copied follower is a plain function word can stay at 0.1-0.2x max. Text where nothing repeats stays at or below 0.2x max (first occurrences, unique prose, and repeated function words such as 'the' or 'and'), except that a run of bare commas or a loose parallel list frame reaches 0.25-0.35x max, and at a context's first token, where no earlier copy exists, it attends to itself — writing near its average unless that token is rare, as a BOM is (0.8x max); the one unrepeated prose case I found above the line is the fixed pair 'Photosynthesis ... converts light into ...' (~0.3x max).
